input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: All calls to the decorated function now share and clear a single statistics dict (wrapped_f.statistics). Previously each call got its own copy.statistics dict. Concurrent or nested/recursive calls will clear and interleave each other's stats.
- rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function is called from multiple threads or recursively. The second call runs stats.clear() and writes into the same dict, wiping the first call's attempt_number and idle_for counters. Result: wrong statistics and potentially corrupted retry bookkeeping. The code comment about avoiding overwrites of local contexts shows this was a deliberate prior design.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label. All calls share one statistics dict that is cleared on each call, so concurrent or nested calls wipe and interleave each other's counters. Both describe stats.clear() in a second call corrupting the first call's attempt_number and related fields, which leaves the statistics wrong.
